lessons.title: Angles on a line
lessons.label: Angles on a line
lessons.objective: Use a straight angle to find a missing adjacent angle.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Calling adjacent angles on a straight line complementary; they sum to 180, not 90.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why must the two angles add to one hundred and eighty degrees?

steps.title: A straight angle is half a turn

left.text: one hundred and eighty degrees
left.spoken: one hundred and eighty degrees

steps.explanation: Angles meeting on this straight line fill a half turn.

scene.description: A half-turn sector measuring one hundred and eighty degrees.

steps.title: Show the known angle

left.text: one hundred and ten degrees plus unknown equals one hundred and eighty degrees
left.spoken: one hundred and ten degrees plus unknown equals one hundred and eighty degrees

steps.explanation: The blue angle is one hundred and ten degrees. The purple angle fills the rest.

scene.description: Adjacent sectors of one hundred and ten degrees and an unknown angle fill the straight angle.

steps.title: Find the rest of the half turn

left.text: one hundred and eighty minus one hundred and ten equals seventy degrees
left.spoken: one hundred and eighty minus one hundred and ten equals seventy degrees

steps.explanation: Subtract the known angle from the straight angle. The missing angle is seventy degrees.

scene.description: The two adjacent angles measure one hundred and ten and seventy degrees.

lessons.title: Rectangle area
lessons.label: Rectangle area
lessons.objective: Connect rows of unit squares to length times width.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Using boundary units instead of square units for area.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why is this answer in square units rather than units?

steps.title: Area measures the inside

left.text: five times three
left.spoken: five times three

steps.explanation: Cover the rectangle with equal unit squares, without gaps or overlaps.

scene.description: A rectangle 5 units wide and 3 units high.

steps.title: Fill row 1

left.text: 1 times five equals 5
left.spoken: 1 times five equals 5

steps.explanation: Each row contains five unit squares. One row covers five square units.

scene.description: 1 complete rows of five shaded unit squares.

steps.title: Fill row 2

left.text: 2 times five equals 10
left.spoken: 2 times five equals 10

steps.explanation: Each row contains five unit squares. 2 rows cover 10 square units.

scene.description: 2 complete rows of five shaded unit squares.

steps.title: Fill row 3

left.text: 3 times five equals 15
left.spoken: 3 times five equals 15

steps.explanation: Each row contains five unit squares. 3 rows cover 15 square units.

scene.description: 3 complete rows of five shaded unit squares.

steps.title: Three rows of five make fifteen

left.text: five times three equals fifteen
left.spoken: five times three equals fifteen

steps.explanation: The area is fifteen square units. Each small square is one square unit.

scene.description: A rectangle 5 units wide and 3 units high.

lessons.title: Angles around a point
lessons.label: Angles around a point
lessons.objective: Use a full turn to find the remaining angle around a point.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Using 180 for a full turn around a point.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: How is a full turn different from a straight angle?

steps.title: Start with the first angle

left.text: one hundred and forty degrees
left.spoken: one hundred and forty degrees

steps.explanation: The first angle covers part of a full turn.

scene.description: A one hundred and forty degree sector.

steps.title: Add the next angle

left.text: one hundred and forty plus ninety equals two hundred and thirty degrees
left.spoken: one hundred and forty plus ninety equals two hundred and thirty degrees

steps.explanation: A right angle adds ninety degrees. Together the known angles cover two hundred and thirty degrees.

scene.description: The two known sectors total two hundred and thirty degrees.

steps.title: Complete the full turn

left.text: three hundred and sixty minus two hundred and thirty equals one hundred and thirty degrees
left.spoken: three hundred and sixty minus two hundred and thirty equals one hundred and thirty degrees

steps.explanation: The remaining angle is one hundred and thirty degrees. The three angles make a full turn.

scene.description: Angles of one hundred and forty, ninety and one hundred and thirty degrees make three hundred and sixty degrees.

lessons.title: Rectangle perimeter
lessons.label: Rectangle perimeter
lessons.objective: Find perimeter by adding all four boundary lengths.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Multiplying length by width gives perimeter.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why must both long sides and both short sides be counted?

steps.title: Perimeter measures the boundary

left.text: six units by four units
left.spoken: six units by four units

steps.explanation: Walk around the outside. Count each of the four sides once.

scene.description: A rectangle 6 units wide and 4 units high.

steps.title: Count the top side

left.text: six
left.spoken: six

steps.explanation: The top side is six units long.

scene.description: A rectangle 6 units wide and 4 units high.

steps.title: Count the right side

left.text: six plus four
left.spoken: six plus four

steps.explanation: The right side is four units long.

scene.description: A rectangle 6 units wide and 4 units high.

steps.title: Count the bottom side

left.text: six plus four plus six
left.spoken: six plus four plus six

steps.explanation: The bottom side is six units long.

scene.description: A rectangle 6 units wide and 4 units high.

steps.title: Count the left side

left.text: six plus four plus six plus four
left.spoken: six plus four plus six plus four

steps.explanation: The left side is four units long.

scene.description: A rectangle 6 units wide and 4 units high.

steps.title: Add all four side lengths

left.text: six plus four plus six plus four equals twenty
left.spoken: six plus four plus six plus four equals twenty

steps.explanation: The perimeter is twenty units. This measures length around the edge, not the space inside.

scene.description: A rectangle 6 units wide and 4 units high.

lessons.title: Triangle area
lessons.label: Triangle area
lessons.objective: Explain the factor one half by completing a rectangle with a congruent triangle.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Using the sloping side instead of the perpendicular height.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why does adding a congruent triangle help us find the area?

steps.title: Start with a right triangle

left.text: base six, perpendicular height four
left.spoken: base six, perpendicular height four

steps.explanation: The base and perpendicular height are six and four units.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular base six and height four.

steps.title: Add one congruent triangle

left.text: six times four equals twenty four
left.spoken: six times four equals twenty four

steps.explanation: A second triangle of exactly the same shape and size completes the rectangle.

scene.description: Two congruent right triangles fill a six by four rectangle.

steps.title: Take half the rectangle

left.text: twenty four divided by two equals twelve
left.spoken: twenty four divided by two equals twelve

steps.explanation: The rectangle has twenty-four square units. Each congruent triangle has half: twelve.

scene.description: Two congruent right triangles fill a six by four rectangle.

lessons.title: Pythagoras: square areas
lessons.label: Pythagoras: square areas
lessons.objective: Connect the two smaller square areas to the hypotenuse square in a three-four-five example.
prerequisites: Square numbers and square roots; recognise a right angle.

tutorNotes.observe: Let the student describe the visible change before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Adding the side lengths directly rather than adding their squares.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why do we compare nine plus sixteen with twenty-five rather than three plus four with five?

steps.title: Find the right angle and hypotenuse

left.text: side lengths three, four and five
left.spoken: side lengths three, four and five

steps.explanation: The perpendicular sides are three and four. The opposite, longest side is five: the hypotenuse c.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 3 and 4, and hypotenuse 5.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Build the first square

left.text: three squared equals nine
left.spoken: three squared equals nine

steps.explanation: The square on the three-unit side has nine unit tiles.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 3 and 4, and hypotenuse 5. Known square areas: a: 9.
scene.caption: Unit tiles show areas; outlines keep their original sizes.

steps.title: Build the second square

left.text: four squared equals sixteen
left.spoken: four squared equals sixteen

steps.explanation: The square on the four-unit side has sixteen unit tiles.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 3 and 4, and hypotenuse 5. Known square areas: a: 9, b: 16.
scene.caption: Unit tiles show areas; outlines keep their original sizes.

steps.title: Build the hypotenuse square

left.text: five squared equals twenty-five
left.spoken: five squared equals twenty-five

steps.explanation: The square on the five-unit hypotenuse has room for twenty-five unit tiles.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 3 and 4, and hypotenuse 5. Known square areas: a: 9, b: 16, c: 25.
scene.caption: Unit tiles show areas; outlines keep their original sizes.

steps.title: Compare the same total area

left.text: nine plus sixteen equals twenty-five
left.spoken: nine plus sixteen equals twenty-five

steps.explanation: Move the nine and sixteen unit tiles into the largest square. They fit without gaps or overlaps; no tile changes size.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 3 and 4, and hypotenuse 5. Known square areas: a: 9, b: 16, c: 25.
scene.caption: Unit tiles show areas; outlines keep their original sizes.

steps.title: State the square-area relationship

left.text: three squared plus four squared equals five squared
left.spoken: three squared plus four squared equals five squared

steps.explanation: Pythagoras relates square areas on a right triangle. This example illustrates the theorem; checking one example is not a general proof.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 3 and 4, and hypotenuse 5. Known square areas: a: 9, b: 16, c: 25.
scene.caption: Unit tiles show areas; outlines keep their original sizes.

lessons.title: Find the hypotenuse
lessons.label: Find the hypotenuse
lessons.objective: Square perpendicular sides, add square areas, then take a positive root.
prerequisites: Understand square areas on a right triangle and principal square roots.

tutorNotes.observe: Let the student describe the visible change before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Stopping at one hundred, or taking the square root before adding areas.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why is one hundred an area, while ten is a length?

steps.title: Identify the unknown longest side

left.text: a equals six, b equals eight, c unknown
left.spoken: a equals six, b equals eight, c unknown

steps.explanation: The unknown c is opposite the marked right angle. It is the hypotenuse.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 6 and 8, and hypotenuse unknown c.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Use the square-area relationship

left.text: six squared plus eight squared equals c squared
left.spoken: six squared plus eight squared equals c squared

steps.explanation: For a right triangle, the two smaller square areas add to the hypotenuse square area.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 6 and 8, and hypotenuse unknown c.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Square the first shorter side

left.text: thirty-six plus eight squared equals c squared
left.spoken: thirty-six plus eight squared equals c squared

steps.explanation: Six squared is thirty-six.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 6 and 8, and hypotenuse unknown c. Known square areas: a: 36.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Square the other shorter side

left.text: thirty-six plus sixty-four equals c squared
left.spoken: thirty-six plus sixty-four equals c squared

steps.explanation: Eight squared is sixty-four.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 6 and 8, and hypotenuse unknown c. Known square areas: a: 36, b: 64.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Add the two square areas

left.text: c squared equals one hundred
left.spoken: c squared equals one hundred

steps.explanation: Thirty-six plus sixty-four is one hundred. This is an area, not the side length.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 6 and 8, and hypotenuse unknown c. Known square areas: a: 36, b: 64, c: 100.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Take the positive square root

left.text: c equals the square root of one hundred, which is ten
left.spoken: c equals the square root of one hundred, which is ten

steps.explanation: The side length is the positive square root of its square area. The hypotenuse is ten units, longer than six or eight.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 6 and 8, and hypotenuse 10. Known square areas: a: 36, b: 64, c: 100.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

lessons.title: Find a shorter side
lessons.label: Find a shorter side
lessons.objective: Subtract a known square area from the hypotenuse square before taking a positive root.
prerequisites: Square roots; subtract the same amount from both sides of an equation.

tutorNotes.observe: Let the student describe the visible change before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Adding twelve squared and thirteen squared when the hypotenuse is already known.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why does this example need subtraction rather than addition?

steps.title: The hypotenuse is already known

left.text: b equals twelve, c equals thirteen, a unknown
left.spoken: b equals twelve, c equals thirteen, a unknown

steps.explanation: Thirteen is the hypotenuse, opposite the right angle. The unknown a is a shorter side.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides unknown a and 12, and hypotenuse 13.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Set up the square areas

left.text: a squared plus twelve squared equals thirteen squared
left.spoken: a squared plus twelve squared equals thirteen squared

steps.explanation: The two smaller squares together have the same area as the hypotenuse square.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides unknown a and 12, and hypotenuse 13.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Square the hypotenuse

left.text: a squared plus twelve squared equals one hundred and sixty-nine
left.spoken: a squared plus twelve squared equals one hundred and sixty-nine

steps.explanation: Thirteen squared is one hundred and sixty-nine.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides unknown a and 12, and hypotenuse 13. Known square areas: c: 169.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Square the known shorter side

left.text: a squared plus one hundred and forty-four equals one hundred and sixty-nine
left.spoken: a squared plus one hundred and forty-four equals one hundred and sixty-nine

steps.explanation: Twelve squared is one hundred and forty-four.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides unknown a and 12, and hypotenuse 13. Known square areas: b: 144, c: 169.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Find the remaining square area

left.text: a squared equals one hundred and sixty-nine minus one hundred and forty-four
left.spoken: a squared equals one hundred and sixty-nine minus one hundred and forty-four

steps.explanation: Subtract one hundred and forty-four from both sides. The unknown square is the remaining part of the hypotenuse square area.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides unknown a and 12, and hypotenuse 13. Known square areas: b: 144, c: 169.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Calculate the difference

left.text: a squared equals twenty-five
left.spoken: a squared equals twenty-five

steps.explanation: One hundred and sixty-nine minus one hundred and forty-four leaves twenty-five square units.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides unknown a and 12, and hypotenuse 13. Known square areas: a: 25, b: 144, c: 169.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Take the positive square root

left.text: a equals square root of twenty-five, which is five
left.spoken: a equals square root of twenty-five, which is five

steps.explanation: The shorter side is five units. We subtracted because one square area was missing from a known total.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 5 and 12, and hypotenuse 13. Known square areas: a: 25, b: 144, c: 169.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.
